question.problem: The function $f(x)=\frac{3}{4+kx}$ has an inverse function given by ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{3-4x}{2x}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{3}{4+kx}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{3}{4+ky}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{3}{4+ky} \\ x(4+ky) & =3 \\ 4x+kxy & =3 \\ kxy & =3-4x \\ y & =\frac{3-4x}{kx}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{3-4x}{kx}.
$$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=2.$
